question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -7 & -5 \\ 1 & 10 & 7 & 2 \\ -1 & 0 & 8 & 7 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -7 & -5 \\ 0 & 13 & 14 & 7 \\ 0 & -3 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & -5 & -14 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary row operations 

- ${R}_{2}:=…$
- ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}$
- ${R}_{4}:=…$

each of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{1},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary row operations?
question.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries below ${a}_{11}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -7 & -5 \\ 1 & 10 & 7 & 2 \\ -1 & 0 & 8 & 7 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -7 & -5 \\ 0 & 13 & 14 & 7 \\ -1 & 0 & 8 & 7 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -7 & -5 \\ 0 & 13 & 14 & 7 \\ 0 & -3 & 1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -7 & -5 \\ 0 & 13 & 14 & 7 \\ 0 & -3 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & -5 & -14 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

  

Therefore, the missing elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-{R}_{1}\,$ and $\,{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+2{R}_{1}.$
